steps.what: List food and beverage deliveries due
Receive the delivery and check contents
Verify product quality and quantity
Sign the delivery check
File the signed delivery check
outputs: filed copy of signed delivery check v1

tasks.design: A job lists food and beverage deliveries in {PROCUREMENT} that are due on the stored delivery date. The manager receives the delivery, checks the contents, and verifies quality and quantity. A later job files the signed check in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Due deliveries were copied before the dock check.
tasks.enabler_now: Order identifier and delivery date are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: Quality is still judged on the dock.
tasks.human_edge: The manager accepts or refuses the delivery.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week on the dock, not on finding due deliveries.

reach.task: Accept only what the manager verified

evidence.claim: The executive digest says budgets and records come from the booking or ledger system, and a person checks the commentary against the figures.

assumptions: Order identifier, item, quantity, and delivery date are stored on the purchasing record. The purchasing record produces them. A delivery is due on the stored delivery date. A blank date is shown as not due.
Native configuration of the purchasing record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the manager signed is filed or sent.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining check is still the manager verifying quality and quantity.

incremental.description: Refresh order identifier and delivery date when the purchasing layout changes, and drop a check the manager has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many delivery dates are blank. The high end assumes order identifier and delivery date are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Propose unnamed prep slots and food totals
Coordinate assignments of cooking personnel
Ensure timely preparation and food use
Sign the cooking assignment
File the signed cooking assignment
outputs: filed copy of signed cooking assignment v1

tasks.design: A job proposes unnamed prep slots and food totals in {HCM} from stored working-time rules. It writes no person name. The manager coordinates the cooking assignments and checks timely preparation. A later job files the signed assignment in {DOCS}. No model is used.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prep grids were drawn before the names were added.
tasks.enabler_now: Slot start, food quantity, and the working-time rule are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The manager still names the cook.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week assigning cooks, not on drawing the grid.

evidence.claim: The executive digest says scheduling is a configured product, and working-time rules are solver constraints. No model.
Digest [S4] describes a vendor shift-planning time. This design does not use that figure as its saving.
Digest [S9] says a staff decision must not rest on automation alone.
Digest [S10] says hiring, evaluating, or rostering staff on behaviour or traits is high-risk.
Digest [S11] says those duties apply from 2 December 2027.
Digest [S12] says rosters and staff monitoring need works-council consent.

assumptions: Slot start, slot end, duty, and food quantity are proposed from the roster record. The roster record produces the working-time rules. A blank rule is shown as a gap and that slot is not proposed. The solver does not write a person name.
Native configuration of the roster record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the manager signed is filed or sent.
Works-council consent for a roster or for monitoring named staff is a separate decision. This design does not treat that consent as already given, and it does not build a camera score of patrons.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining assignment time is still the manager coordinating cooking personnel.

incremental.description: Refresh slot start, food quantity, and working-time rule when the roster layout changes, and drop an assignment the manager has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes a working-time rule is blank, so that slot is not proposed. The high end assumes slot start, food quantity, and the rule are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train, hire, and evaluate in person.

steps.what: List stored training sessions, not scores
Organize and direct worker training programs
Resolve personnel problems and hire staff
Evaluate employee performance in dining facilities
Sign the staffing note
File the signed staffing note
outputs: filed copy of signed staffing note v1

tasks.design: A job lists stored training sessions in {LMS}. It does not score a person. The manager organizes and directs the training, resolves personnel problems, hires staff, and evaluates employee performance in person. A later job files the signed note in {DOCS}. The evaluation is not a rule about a person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training dates were recopied before the meeting.
tasks.enabler_now: Course identifier and date are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: Hiring and evaluation stay with the manager.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides whom to hire and how the work went.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week with people, not on listing courses.

reach.task: Attend only the session the manager directs

steps.what: List unnamed hours that are still open
Assess staffing needs from those hours
Recruit by attendance at job fairs
Sign the newspaper advertisement
Send only the signed advertisement
outputs: filed copy of signed advertisement v1

tasks.design: A job lists unnamed open hours in {HCM}. The manager assesses staffing needs and recruits by attendance at job fairs or by a newspaper advertisement. A later job sends only the signed advertisement by {EMAIL}. It does not rank candidates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Open hours were copied before the fair.
tasks.enabler_now: Duty and open hours are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The conversation at the fair stays with the manager.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides the wording and whom to speak with.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week recruiting, not on totalling hours.

Digest [S12] says rosters and staff monitoring need works-council consent.

assumptions: Duty, open hours, and site are stored on the roster record. The roster record produces them. A blank hour stays blank and is not treated as a vacancy.

role.altitude: The food service manager spends the week on the floor, the guest, and the signed decision. A stored total, a working-time slot with no name, and filing that decision can move. The manager still counts the cash, tastes the food, and assigns the names.
reach: A cook follows only the assignment the manager signed.
A supplier receives only the order the manager signed.
skills_to_grow: Reject a roster slot that already contains a person name.
Reject a total that does not match the stored rows.
Reject an order that the manager has not signed.
role.ambitious_version: A signed roster or order can be filed the same week, and the manager still owns the floor.
